# BINDING CONSISTENCY LEDGER — Danish Listening Pod (15 scenes)

## 1. TRANSLITERATION
Not needed — names stay as written. (Danish uses Latin alphabet; all personal names — Sarah, James, Anna, Davies, Jones — and place names — Manchester, London, France — remain unchanged.)

## 2. PRICES
- £8.40 → 65 kroner
- £12.50 → 95 kroner

## 3. TARGET-LANGUAGE NAME
dansk

## 4. RECURRING LINES

| Canonical | Danish rendering |
|-----------|------------------|
| Good morning. What can I get you? | Godmorgen. Hvad kan jeg få for dig? |
| Good afternoon. | God eftermiddag. |
| Thank you very much. Goodbye. | Mange tak. Farvel. |
| Could I pay by card? | Kan jeg betale med kort? |
| Do you have contactless? | Har du kontaktløst? |
| Yes, of course. | Ja, selvfølgelig. |
| Excuse me. | Undskyld. |
| You've been very helpful. | Du har været meget hjælpsom. |
| I'm learning Danish. | Jeg lærer dansk. |
| Good evening. What can I get you? | God aften. Hvad kan jeg få for dig? |
| Would you like to sit-in or takeaway? | Skal det være her eller med ud? |
| Is everything alright? | Er alt i orden? |
| I'm on holiday. | Jeg er på ferie. |
| Thank you. | Tak. |

## 5. REGISTER
Use **du** universally (customer–staff, strangers, friends). Politeness signalled through phrase choice and tone, not grammatical formality. No honorifics. Natural requests: *Jeg vil gerne have…* or *Kan jeg få…* Softeners (*lige*, *bare*, *faktisk*) used sparingly and naturally. Response to thanks: *Selv tak* or *Det var så lidt*.
